log.note: Read backlog/items/2026-08-19-publication-authority-lacks-execution-time-criticalproof-reverification.md (triaged needs-PO-decision), critical-action-authorization.mjs (authorizeRecordedPush/authorizeRecordedDeploy), guard-push.mjs's enforcePublicationAuthorization, publication-authority.mjs, publication-executor.mjs, and pipeline-state.mjs's publication-approve subcommand.

guard-push.mjs's enforcePublicationAuthorization (lines 937-977) unconditionally calls emit(2, [...]) at line 942 -- emit() is process.exit(code), executed before ANY of the subsequent validation logic runs. The function's own comment (line 946-951) confirms this: 'The validation below remains intentionally unreachable during the schema migration window... no raw command can cross the new executor-only boundary.' So guard-push.mjs's publication branch NEVER permits a publication push through; it categorically blocks and points at 'the plugin-owned fixed publication executor'. There is no location inside guard-push.mjs that gates the real external effect for publication -- the DoD's premise that 'guard-push.mjs's publication enforcement path calls it immediately before permitting the real external effect' does not hold.

Traced the actual push: publication-executor.mjs's executePublication() (line 763) calls beginPublicationExecutionAuthority (publication-authority.mjs:272, in-scope) at line 795, then performs the real runGit(['push', ...]) at lines 812-823 -- all inside publication-executor.mjs, which is NOT in the briefing's Forbidden-section touch list. beginPublicationExecutionAuthority is the last authority checkpoint before the push and would be the correct mirror-point in spirit.

beginPublicationExecutionAuthority's entire input surface is {gitCommonDir, transactionId, channel, expectedRawSha256, expectedRevision, expectedStateSha256, attemptId, executorSha256, startedAt, heldLocks} -- a git-object-backed CAS store scoped by gitCommonDir. It has NO dependency on project/pipeline-state.json (the JSON `state` authorizeRecordedPush/authorizeRecordedDeploy read `criticalProof` from) and NO dependency on project/critical-human-proof.json (the anchorDir critical-action-authorization.mjs reads trust anchors from). publication-executor.mjs's entire call chain (physicalRepository/readPublicationAuthority) is deliberately isolated to this git-object CAS store -- confirmed by its own design (freshAlternatesDisabledReadback, 'fresh-disposable' repositoryKind, alternatesDisabled:true) which exists specifically to minimize what the executor trusts. Wiring in a re-verification would require teaching this isolated executor to newly read and trust a mutable JSON file (project/pipeline-state.json) it has never depended on -- a genuine trust-boundary change to publication-executor.mjs (out of scope) or a schema migration moving criticalProof into the git-object-backed authority record itself (exactly Direction 1 from the filed backlog item, which the item's own triage calls 'a non-trivial schema migration touching a gate-strength-adjacent execution boundary').

This matches Stop Condition 5 ("the CAS transaction model is structurally incompatible with the commit/tree-based subject push/deploy use") verbatim, not on the {commit,tree} subject shape (which IS compatible -- 'publication' is already a valid CRITICAL_ACTION_KINDS member and prior.candidateOid/candidateTree already exist), but on the verification-time INPUT SURFACE: authorizeRecordedPush/Deploy assume the caller already holds the JSON pipeline-state.json and can read project/critical-human-proof.json from anchorDir -- both true at guard-push.mjs's push/deploy call sites, both absent from publication-executor.mjs's entire trust chain by deliberate design. No code was changed; stopping per the briefing's explicit stop condition rather than forcing an incompatible mirror or expanding scope past the Forbidden list.
